title: QBR KPI mini-workshop handout: operational metric definitions & quick tables
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, meeting-friendly reference for CS managers running QBRs that focus on the operational economics signals we care about: latency, uptime, cost/token, and cache hit rate. Use it as a one-page cheat sheet in pre-QBR workshops, hand it to engineering partners, or paste into the QBR deck notes.

Notes on scope and audience:
- Audience: CS leads, Solutions Engineering, SRE/Platform oncall, and account execs.
- Scope: Production serving KPIs (hosted + dedicated) that drive renewal conversations and technical remediation. Not a model quality doc (separate evals).
- Measurement window: default rolling 30-day for trend, 7-day for recent SLO checks; include 24-hr for incident context.

Metric definitions (plain English + measurement guidance):
1) Latency (per-request token generation latency)
   - Definition: Time between service ingress (request accepted) and the first response byte (stream-start) and time to final token. We track two numbers: "start latency" (first-byte) and "completion latency" (final-byte) on a per-request basis.
   - Units: milliseconds (ms). Aggregates: p50, p90, p95, p99 over the measurement window.
   - Calculation notes: Exclude requests that timed out or were cancelled by client from median/percentile calculations but report counts separately. When comparing with customer SLAs, always use trimmed percentiles (exclude top 0.1% extreme outliers) if there was a global outage.
   - Common pitfalls: variable prompt lengths should be normalized (report latency per 1k input+output tokens as an additional normalization). For streaming routes, include both time-to-first-byte and average inter-token latency.

2) Uptime (service availability)
   - Definition: Percentage of successful request attempts over total accepted requests for a route, where successful = returns a 2xx or valid streaming session end. Internal definition excludes client-side network failures.
   - Units: percentage (%). Aggregates: daily availability, rolling-30-day availability. Convert to minutes of downtime per month for customer conversations.
   - SLO example: 99.95% monthly availability = ~21.6 minutes downtime/mo. For Dedicated customers with contractual SLAs, use the contract's measurement window.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
   - Definition: total serving cost divided by total tokens served (input+output tokens) for the measurement window. Serving cost = GPU runtime + memory overhead + amortized infra + cache storage egress where applicable.
   - Units: USD per 1k tokens (we use per-1k to keep numbers readable).
   - Calculation guidance: use billing-aligned cost model (hours * hourly GPU cost + amortized infra for the same window). Exclude one-time transfer or onboarding costs. For multi-tenant hosted customers, use usage-tagged cost buckets when possible.
   - Notes: present both raw cost/token and normalized cost/token (by sequence length bucket e.g., 0-128, 129-512, 512+). This highlights cost drivers.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix & KV cache)
   - Definition: percentage of requests (or tokens) served without invoking full model compute because a cache entry satisfied the request (prefix/KV cache).
   - Units: percentage (%). Report both request-level hit-rate and token-level hit-rate.
   - Calculation: cache_hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses). Distinguish between warm-cache and cold-start windows (first 30 minutes after restart).
   - Implications: higher cache hit rate reduces cost and tail latency. When reporting, include estimated cost savings = hit_rate * average_compute_cost_reduction.

KPI reporting table (compact CSV-style — copy into spreadsheet)
Columns: Metric, Window, Aggregation, Value, Threshold (green/amber/red), Notes
KPI_ROWS_START
Latency (start ms),30d,p50,45,green:<100ms;amber:100-250ms;red:>250ms,Normalized to 1k tokens
Latency (start ms),30d,p95,180,green:<200ms;amber:200-400ms;red:>400ms,Review batching and model size
Latency (completion ms),30d,p99,1200,green:<1s;amber:1-2s;red:>2s,Impact on interactive apps
Uptime (%),30d,rolling,99.96,green:>=99.95;amber:99.9-99.95;red:<99.9,Convert to downtime mins/mo when talking to customers
Cost per 1k tokens,30d,avg,3.40,green:<5;amber:5-10;red:>10,Show normalized by length bucket
Cache hit rate (request),30d,avg,28%,green:>=25%;amber:10-25%;red:<10%,Estimate CPU/GPU savings and reduced p99 latency
Cache hit rate (token),30d,avg,41%,green:>=35%;amber:20-35%;red:<20%,Token-level matters for long completions
KPI_ROWS_END

Pre-QBR checklist (what CS should gather and send to engineering 72 hrs before QBR):
- Top 10 routes by volume and by cost (CSV)
- Recent 30/7/1-day latency percentiles per route (p50/p95/p99)
- Uptime dashboard link and incident list (last 90 days)
- Cost/token breakdown by sequence-length buckets and model variant
- Cache metrics: warm vs cold hit rates, eviction/TTL patterns
- Any ongoing rollouts or model changes scheduled in next 30 days

Suggested remediation playbook snippets (short action items):
- High p95/p99 completion latency: enable micro-batching for high-throughput routes, check KV cache warmup, validate quantization profile for the model.
- Elevated cost/token with low cache hit rate: run prompt normalization project + increase cache TTL for stable responses; consider routing to smaller model for short completions.
- Uptime dips: check autoscaler error logs and capacity throttles, review recent deploys, validate fallback policies to a safe model variant.

Customer-facing talking points (how to explain common signals succinctly):
- Latency: "We measure the time to first token and to final token. P95 tells us how often customers see lag — we aim to keep P95 within your app's interactive budget."
- Cost/token: "Shown per 1k tokens and normalized by response size. We'll call out improvements we can make (cache, batching, smaller model variants) and quantify $/month delta."
- Cache hit rate: "Higher hit rate means fewer GPU cycles and faster responses for repeated or templated prompts. We'll show estimated dollars saved and propose TTL adjustments."

Sample QBR agenda (30-45 minutes):
1) Executive TL;DR (3 min): top health signals, renewal risk flag (green/amber/red)
2) KPI snapshot (7 min): show the KPI table above and call out trends
3) Incidents & reliability (8 min): recent outages, mitigations, remaining risk
4) Cost & optimization (8 min): cost/token drivers, cache wins, quick wins + roadmap
5) Action items & owners (5 min): list 3 high-impact items, owners, and target dates

Retro prompts (if metrics looked worse than expected):
- What changed in traffic mix in the last 30 days?
- Any recent model rollouts or config changes?
- Which route(s) contributed most to P95 growth?
- Which of our suggested optimizations are quickest to pilot?

Workshop exercises (use in pre-QBR working session):
- Exercise A: Given route-level table, identify 3 routes for targeted cache TTL increase and estimate cost savings (15 min).
- Exercise B: Given latency by length-bucket, propose two model-routing rules (route A -> small model for <128 tokens; route B -> large model for long responses) and estimate delta cost and expected QoS impact (20 min).

Appendix: short formulas (copyable)
- request_cache_hit_rate = requests_served_from_cache / total_requests
- token_cache_hit_rate = tokens_served_from_cache / total_tokens
- cost_per_1k_tokens = (total_serving_cost_usd / total_tokens) * 1000
- downtime_minutes_per_month = (1 - uptime_fraction) * 60 * 24 * 30

Footer notes: this is a working handout — keep a copy in the QBR folder, link to the canonical KPI dashboards in Confluence before the meeting. If you want a slide-ready version, request from product-ops (Confluence link in linked artifacts).
